findings.issue: `pkill -f "entry.node-server"` matched the agent's own bash command, killing the shell (exit 143) — repeated at turns 61, 77 and 81
findings.suggestion: Kill by recorded PID (it already wrote /tmp/app.pid) or by port (`fuser -k 3000/tcp`), never by a pattern that matches the invoking command line

findings.issue: TypeScript is a devDependency with a hand-written tsconfig, but tsc was never run; the vite build only strips types
findings.suggestion: Add a `tsc --noEmit` typecheck step and run it before declaring done

findings.issue: Three turns spent grepping for typos (`</d>`, `labelledby`) that it had never actually made — no new information gained
findings.suggestion: Trust the write results and let the build/tests catch real problems

findings.issue: No use of web search, docs, skills or MCP for the Qwik APIs; relied on reading installed .d.ts files
findings.suggestion: A quick doc check for adapter/entry scaffolding would have been cheaper and less fragile than inferring the template from type declarations

findings.issue: Visual comparison covered home, pokemon, pokemon-moves, type, types, move and mobile home, but not the ability, not-found or home-filtered pages
findings.suggestion: Screenshot every page listed in the spec's design table, since layout regressions there wouldn't be caught by the a11y-focused tests

summary: A near-model session: the agent front-loaded empirical verification of every spec and data assumption, wrote the whole app in a single pass, and passed all 54 acceptance tests on its first run with zero fix cycles. It then went beyond the tests with screenshot comparisons against the design references, edge-case URL probes, and a final clean re-run after its last edit. The only real waste was process hygiene — three separate self-inflicted `pkill` kills and ~6 lost turns restarting dev servers — plus a missing typecheck.
